operations: Opened official RFC 5545 HTML at cited sections on TZID/VTIMEZONE, explicit and recurrence-generated gaps, RECURRENCE-ID compatibility, UID, recurrence-set composition, and unknown values/properties.
Opened docs.rs rrule2 latest documentation page, which identified version 0.15.0, at its DTSTART and DST behavior notes. The version-pinned web URL returned an internal error.
independent_recheck.result: Confirmed RFC distinguishes explicit nonexistent local date-time resolution from recurrence-generated nonexistent instance omission. Confirmed rrule2 0.15.0 documentation describes the pre-gap offset for generated instances, so the predecessor broad RFC-style characterization is rejected.
independent_recheck.validation_boundary: Documentation research only. No downloaded code, parser, recurrence engine, provider API, import/export, SQLite mutation, or round-trip test was run.

dispositions.resolution: The final specifies RRULE allow-list: FREQ=WEEKLY; optional INTERVAL=1; optional one matching unnumbered BYDAY; rejects COUNT, UNTIL, WKST, other BY parts, EXRULE, multiple RRULEs, mismatches, and RDATE PERIOD as stated.
Require matching RECURRENCE-ID value type and local-time form/TZID; validate RDATE/EXDATE temporal type and TZID under same profile.
Correct the rrule2 characterization; unqualify the candidate for this rule until adapter or version-pinned behavior is demonstrated.

Separate RFC’s unknown VALUE data preservation requirement from its permission for readers to ignore unknown IANA/X properties; the brief independently prohibits silent loss, so retain or block export.
External EXDATE plus detached override composition, intended-zone equivalence of supplied VTIMEZONE, and candidate parser/writer/engine behavior remain unverified.

sources.title: RFC 5545: Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar)
sources.locator: §3.2.19 (TZID), lines 1435-1497; §3.2.20 (VALUE data types), lines 1539-1550; §3.3.5 (explicit local date-time fold/gap), lines 1791-1807; §3.3.10 (generated invalid/nonexistent instances), lines 2277-2281; §3.6.5 (VTIMEZONE coverage), lines 3456-3475; §3.8.4.4 (RECURRENCE-ID original slot and type/local-time compatibility), lines 6022-6078; §3.8.4.7 (UID), lines 6264-6312; §3.8.5.1 (EXDATE precedence and DTSTART retention), lines 6368-6392; §3.8.5.3 (RRULE, set composition, synchronization), lines 6534-6585; §3.8.8.1-.2 (IANA/X properties), lines 7496-7558
sources.observed_operation: Reviser opened the official RFC HTML directly at the listed sections; the source maps from both prior stages were also read completely. Documentation review only; no implementation executed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: TZID identifies a matching VTIMEZONE; local DATE-TIME without TZID is floating. An explicit ambiguous local date-time means the first fold occurrence; an explicit nonexistent local date-time uses the pre-gap offset. A recurrence-generated nonexistent local instance MUST be ignored and MUST NOT be counted. A recurring component’s VTIMEZONE MUST supply valid information for all recurrence instances. RECURRENCE-ID must match DTSTART value type and local-time form and preserves the original nominal slot when moved. The recurrence set gathers DTSTART/RRULE/RDATE, subtracts EXDATE (which takes precedence), and coalesces duplicate inclusions; unsynchronized DTSTART/RRULE and multiple RRULEs yield undefined recurrence sets. UID is persistent/global identity. Unknown x-name/iana-token VALUE data must be preserved uninterpreted; §3.8.8 allows generic consumers to ignore unknown IANA/X properties.
sources.applicability: Primary authority for .ics recurrence, identity, timezone, explicit/generated DST, and value-preservation semantics. It neither qualifies a Rust implementation nor specifies Google/Graph API behavior.
sources.revision_correction: The predecessor wording blurred unrecognized VALUE data types and unknown X/IANA properties. The RFC mandates retaining unknown VALUE-type data, while the product brief itself supplies the stronger no-silent-drop requirement for opaque properties.

sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The docs say an unsynchronized DTSTART is not force-added by the crate while RFC leaves the result undefined and Google emits it. The page says a recurrence-generated nonexistent spring-gap time uses the pre-gap offset (example: Europe/London 01:30 GMT becomes 02:30 BST), while RFC 5545 §3.3.10 says such a generated instance is ignored and not counted. It also documents earlier-fold handling, Chrono-Tz-supported zones, date ranges, and iteration limits. These are documentation claims; the implementation was not tested.
sources.applicability: Unqualified recurrence candidate. Its documented generated-gap behavior conflicts with the governing RFC policy required by this proposal; no claim is made about runtime behavior beyond the docs.
